title: Identify the game's song clock
acceptance: Documented function(s) that compute current song time/beat and their time source
notes: Song time = XAudio voice samples played / rate + 0.045 s (0x82077100, 0x82080B00); see docs/TIMING.md

title: Native low-latency music path
acceptance: Songs pre-decoded to PCM and played via WASAPI (SDL3); reported output latency < 20 ms
notes: Demoted from P0: sync is solved by compensating the host audio queue (R-204). Only worth doing for lower sound latency; --audio_maxqframes=4 already halves the queue

title: Audio-clock-driven beat timeline
acceptance: Song time follows the music actually being played; no drift over a full song
notes: Done: song clock = XAudio voice position minus the host audio queue (audio_maxqframes x 5.33 ms, default 42.7 ms), --audio_sync_compensation (src/song_clock.cpp, docs/TIMING.md). User A/B test 2026-11-10: new behaviour feels good

title: Global audio offset setting (ms)

notes: --audio_offset_ms works (default -20; user found -15..-25 best on USB headset). Still needs exposing in the settings menu (R-414)

title: Input latency offset setting (ms)
acceptance: Separate input offset shifts judgement windows only
notes: Done: Input Offset in BBRR Settings > Calibration (--input_offset_ms, -100..100) shifts the press span used by the judging function 0x82066700; auto calibration sets it with the audio offset. Play-tested 2026-11-10: arrows stay with the music, only judging moves.

title: Calibration screen (tap to the beat)

notes: First version (untested): BBRR Settings > Calibration (ui_scripts/Options/BBRR_calibrate.lua): 12 taps to clicks, 12 taps to a ring lining up; audio offset = (sound lateness - picture lateness) - host audio queue. Picture lateness is logged for the future input offset (R-206)

notes: 120 and 144 fps play correctly. Frame-locked code found and fixed so far: fade timer (0x821D4330) and the fail slow-down step (0x821A0794, fix untested). Particle/camera code still needs a visual check; replay test not built.

title: Fixed-step sim with render interpolation
acceptance: Simulation at 60 Hz, camera/particles interpolated per frame

title: Frame pacing matched to the display
acceptance: No frame-rate setting needed: the game runs at the display's refresh rate with each frame started on a real display refresh; no judder; optional unlimited mode
notes: Untested: guest refresh rate = main display refresh (src/settings.cpp ApplyFrameRate); SDK patch 0002 ticks the guest vblank from the desktop compositor (DwmFlush) with an evenly spaced timer fallback and no millisecond sleeps in the GPU wait. Before: 120 fps limit gave 5.5-12 ms frame times (judder) on a 120 Hz display

title: Low-latency presentation
acceptance: Flip-model swapchain, waitable object, max 1 frame queued

title: High-rate timestamped input
acceptance: Input polled >= 1 kHz on its own thread; presses timestamped against audio clock
notes: --precise_input (default on): controller read every 1 ms on its own thread; a press is judged at the song time the button went down, keeping one 60 Hz frame of leeway. A press is used only by the first frame that judges after it. XInput pads only. Play-tested 2026-11-11 (felt good); far-off hits are logged for follow-up.
